The catchment area of the Aubach spring varies significantly with hydrologic conditions, reflecting the complex nature of the karst system.  The delineated catchment represents the maximum extent (ca. 29 km²) during low-flow conditions, when the estavelle upstream in the Schwarzwasser valley functions as a sink. In this state, water from the non-karstic, Flysch-dominated catchment of the Schwarzwasser River—primarily from the right side of the valley—is sinking into the karst system. However, not all allogenic recharge entering the estavelle, nor all autogenic recharge from the karstic Gottesacker plateau, discharges at the Aubach spring. A portion of this flow continues through the karst system and emerges at the perennial Sägebach spring and at two smaller springs. During high-flow conditions, the hydraulic behavior of the estavelle reverses and it functions as a spring. In this mode, it acts as an additional outlet of the karst system, and the allogenic catchment (ca. 9 km²) no longer contributes to discharge at the Aubach spring.
